issues.title: IP conflict on 192.168.0.41
issues.detail: 2 different devices answered for 192.168.0.41. Both will lose network randomly, and scanners will show this IP with a changing name/MAC.
issues.fix: One of them has a manually typed IP. Change it to automatic (DHCP), or give it an IP outside the router's DHCP range. Then reserve that IP for it on the router.

issues.title: Very high multicast traffic (1400.0/second)
issues.detail: Not a loop. Multicast this high usually comes from CCTV cameras / an NVR streaming in multicast, or IPTV. Switches without IGMP snooping copy it to every port, which slows Wi-Fi, old PCs and printers.
issues.fix: Set the cameras / NVR to unicast streaming (or turn multicast off). Turn on IGMP snooping: MikroTik /interface bridge set [find] igmp-snooping=yes, and on managed switches. Then re-scan.

issues.title: 1 IP address(es) now used by a different device
issues.detail: Compared with the previous scan. Normal when a device's DHCP lease expires; if the old device is still on the network with a manual IP, it is a conflict waiting to happen.
issues.fix: If it keeps changing, reserve fixed IPs on the router for important devices.

issues.title: 3 device(s) use randomized MACs
issues.detail: These change MAC per network or over time, so other scanners show them as new devices again and again.
issues.fix: For office laptops switch random MAC off for the office Wi-Fi.

issues.title: Bound device SALES-PC is on 192.168.0.70 instead of 192.168.0.87
issues.detail: Its IP was reserved on the router, but the device uses another address. Either the binding commands were not pasted (or were pasted on another router), or the device has a hand-typed IP, or it has not renewed its IP since.
issues.fix: Keep 192.168.0.87: IP-MAC binding tab > tick it > Make router commands (they keep 192.168.0.87) > paste in WinBox, then set the device to automatic (DHCP) and renew its IP ('ipconfig /renew', or unplug / re-plug it). Want 192.168.0.70 instead: tick 'Moved devices: bind their NEW IP' before Make router commands. Not needed any more: select it and 'Forget binding of selected'.

checks.name: Router device list
checks.detail: the router's device list could not be read - sleeping phones, phone names and other networks may be missed. Save the router login in Setup (or Setup > Copy router commands turns on SNMP)

findings.title: IP conflict on 192.168.0.41
actions: One of them has a manually typed IP. Change it to automatic (DHCP), or give it an IP outside the router's DHCP range. Then reserve that IP for it on the router.

missing: Packet sniffer is off - install Npcap and build with Scapy for the loop echo test and the list of devices sending broadcasts.
Monitor has run only 0 min - intermittent problems need time to show up.

alerts.text: 192.168.0.203: XMeye DVR is reachable from the internet - attackers constantly try its logins (45.79.125.182 port 34567)
alerts.title: 192.168.0.203 can be opened from the internet
alerts.why: A port forward or UPnP on the router lets anyone on the internet reach this device. DVRs, cameras and remote desktop get hacked within days (password guessing, known firmware bugs).
alerts.fix: Close the port forward / UPnP (button below); watch the cameras through the maker's app or a VPN instead.
steps: Press 'Close internet access to this device': the router's port forwards to it are disabled and UPnP is turned off.
Log in to the DVR / device and change the admin password (long, not the default).
Update the DVR / camera firmware from the maker's website.
For viewing from outside use the maker's mobile app (cloud / P2P ID) or a VPN - not a port forward.
Re-check: the alert should not return.
fixes: Close internet access to this device

alerts.title: Torrent download on 192.168.0.48
alerts.why: A torrent program (uTorrent, BitTorrent, qBittorrent, Transmission...) downloads and uploads to hundreds of strangers. It fills the internet line for everyone, brings malware and pirated files, and port 51413 / 6881 traffic is what ISPs and copyright notices look for.
alerts.fix: Block torrents on the router (button below) and remove the torrent program from that PC.
steps: Press 'Block torrents on the router': torrent traffic and torrent websites are blocked for every device (Undo is in Tools > Network guard).
Go to the PC at 192.168.0.48 (Inventory shows its name and user).
Control Panel > Programs > uninstall uTorrent / BitTorrent / qBittorrent / Transmission / BitComet; also close it in the taskbar tray.
Run a Windows Defender quick scan on that PC (torrent downloads often carry malware).
Tell the user it is not allowed on the office network.

alerts.title: Critical device not answering: ACCOUNTS-PC (192.168.0.1) - check its power and c
alerts.why: See the root-cause analysis for the details.
alerts.fix: Open Root cause for the most likely cause and its fix.
steps: Press 'Open Root cause' below - Network Doctor checks everything and lists the most likely cause first.
Follow the fix shown there; then press Re-check here.

alerts.title: Router or internet not answering
alerts.why: The router or the internet line stopped answering.
alerts.fix: Check power and cables first, then the internet provider.
steps: Look at the router: power light on? If not, check the adapter / UPS and restart it.
Check the internet cable (from the ISP box / ONT) is in the router's WAN port (ether1) and its light blinks.
Look at the ISP's fibre box (ONT): a red LOS light = fibre problem, call the ISP.
Press 'Test from this PC' below to see where it stops.
Still down after 5 minutes: restart the ONT, wait 2 minutes, then the router.
pc_fixes: Test from this PC: ping -n 4 192.168.0.1 & ping -n 4 8.8.8.8 & nslookup google.com & tracert -d -h 8 8.8.8.8

alerts.text: dhcp,warning Detected conflict by ARP response for 192.168.0.70 from F8:75:A4:8D:B7:FA
alerts.title: IP 192.168.0.70 is typed by hand on F8:75:A4:8D:B7:FA inside the router's DHCP range
alerts.why: The router wanted to give 192.168.0.70 to a device, but F8:75:A4:8D:B7:FA already uses it with a manually typed (static) IP. The router skips it now, but when that device is off the router can hand the same IP to a phone - then both lose the network.
alerts.fix: Reserve 192.168.0.70 for F8:75:A4:8D:B7:FA on the router (the button below) - or switch the device to automatic IP.
steps: Press 'Reserve 192.168.0.70 for this device' below: the router keeps 192.168.0.70 only for F8:75:A4:8D:B7:FA.
Or, if the device does not need a fixed IP: on that device set the IP to automatic (Windows: Settings > Network > Ethernet > IP assignment > Automatic (DHCP)).
Run 'Re-check' after a few minutes: the conflict message should not come back.

alerts.title: A lot of multicast / broadcast traffic
alerts.why: Cameras, IPTV or discovery traffic sent to every port. Not an outage, but slows Wi-Fi.
alerts.fix: Turn on IGMP snooping so multicast only goes where it is wanted.
steps: Press 'Turn on IGMP snooping'.
If it goes on: Live monitor > the device sending most broadcasts; check that camera / NVR.
Managed switches: enable IGMP snooping and storm control too.

alerts.title: Two devices use the same IP 192.168.0.41
alerts.why: Two devices answer for one IP. Both get cut off at random; printers and ERP sessions drop.
alerts.fix: Give each device its own IP: switch the one with the hand-typed IP to automatic, or bind each MAC to its IP (IP-MAC binding).
steps: Note the two MAC addresses in the alert (3C:52:82:01:02:04, 3C:52:82:01:02:99).
Open IP-MAC binding (button below): it shows which device the IP belongs to.
On the other device set the IP to automatic, or change it to a free IP outside the DHCP range.
Restart that device's network (unplug the cable 10 seconds, or ipconfig /renew).
Re-check: the conflict line disappears.
pc_fixes: Clear this PC's ARP / DNS cache: arp -d * & ipconfig /flushdns

commands.name: My IP, MAC, gateway and DHCP details
commands.use: First thing to check: shows this PC's IP, MAC (Physical Address), DHCP on/off and lease times.

commands.name: Get a new IP from the router
commands.use: After a reservation was made, an IP conflict, or 'no internet'.

commands.name: Clear DNS cache
commands.use: Websites open the wrong place or not at all.

commands.name: Show ARP table (IP -> MAC this PC knows)
commands.use: Two IPs with the same MAC, or the router IP with a strange MAC, means a conflict or ARP spoofing.

commands.name: Clear ARP table
commands.use: After fixing a conflict or a spoofing attack (admin).

commands.name: Ping a device non-stop
commands.use: Watch for 'Request timed out' - drops every few minutes point to cable, Wi-Fi or a loop.

commands.name: Ping the router non-stop
commands.use: Is the LAN itself stable? Should be 1-2 ms on cable.

commands.name: Trace the route
commands.use: Where on the way a connection stops.

commands.name: Packet-loss test per hop
commands.use: Finds which hop loses packets (takes ~1 min).

commands.name: Computer name and MAC of a Windows PC
commands.use: Identify an unknown Windows device by its IP.

commands.name: MAC addresses of this PC's adapters
commands.use: For tagging / reservations.

commands.name: Programs with network connections
commands.use: Shows remote addresses and the PID of the program (match PID in Task Manager).

commands.name: Wi-Fi details (signal, band, BSSID)
commands.use: Weak signal (<60%) causes drops that look like network faults.

commands.name: Switch adapter to automatic IP (DHCP)
commands.cmd: netsh interface ipv4 set address name="{adapter}" source=dhcp
commands.use: Removes a manually typed IP (the usual cause of IP conflicts). Adapter name from 'ipconfig'.

commands.name: Lock the router's MAC (anti-NetCut)
commands.cmd: netsh interface ipv4 add neighbors interface="{adapter}" address={gw} neighbor={gw_mac_dash} store=persistent
commands.use: Stops ARP spoofing against this PC. Undo when the router is replaced.

commands.name: Remove the router MAC lock
commands.cmd: netsh interface ipv4 delete neighbors interface="{adapter}" address={gw}
commands.use: Undo of the line above.

commands.name: Reset the network stack
commands.cmd: netsh winsock reset && netsh int ip reset
commands.use: Last resort when networking is broken on one PC (restart afterwards).

commands.name: Open Wi-Fi settings (random addresses)
commands.use: Turn 'Random hardware addresses' off by hand.

commands.name: Is a service reachable? (test a TCP port)
commands.use: TcpTestSucceeded True = the port is open from this PC (e.g. 80 web, 445 file sharing, 3389 Remote Desktop, 1433 SQL / ERP database).

commands.name: Cable speed and duplex of this PC
commands.use: 100 Mbps on a cable = damaged cable / old switch; FullDuplex False = speed set by hand somewhere.

commands.name: Network card error counters
commands.use: Errors that keep growing = bad cable, connector or port.

commands.name: Routing table
commands.use: Two 0.0.0.0 routes (cable + Wi-Fi, or a VPN) = traffic may go out the wrong way.

commands.name: MTU of each adapter
commands.use: Normal 1500. Use Tools > MTU finder to test the whole path.

commands.name: Look up a name (DNS)
commands.use: Which DNS server answers and which IP it gives. 'Non-existent domain' / timeout = DNS problem.

commands.name: Shared folders of a PC / NAS
commands.use: Lists what a PC or NAS shares.

commands.name: Firewall on or off (all profiles)
commands.use: If the PC is on 'Public' profile in the office, sharing and remote tools are blocked.

commands.name: Network category (Private / Public)
commands.use: Office network should be Private. Change: Set-NetConnectionProfile -InterfaceAlias Ethernet -NetworkCategory Private

commands.name: Sync the clock with the internet
commands.use: Wrong PC time breaks HTTPS sites, domain logins and ERP licences. Needs administrator.

commands.name: Wi-Fi drop report (last 3 days)
commands.use: Makes an HTML report of every Wi-Fi disconnect and why (opens from C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\WlanReport).

commands.name: Which router port is a device on?
commands.use: 'on-interface' shows the port (e.g. ether2) - tag the device / switch with it for the map.

commands.name: DHCP lease of a device
commands.cmd: /ip dhcp-server lease print detail where mac-address={mac}
commands.use: Shows its IP, host name, status and whether it is reserved (static).

commands.name: Reserve the current IP for a device (bind)
commands.cmd: :do {/ip dhcp-server lease remove [find where mac-address={mac}]} on-error={}; /ip dhcp-server lease add address={ip} mac-address={mac} comment="ND: {name}"
commands.use: The device keeps DHCP and always gets this IP. Use the Binding tab for many devices at once.

commands.name: Remove a device's reservation
commands.use: Before giving the IP to another device.

commands.name: Find the IP of a MAC
Port link status and speed
commands.use: Speed 10M / half duplex = bad cable or port.

commands.name: Port error counters (bad cable)
commands.use: Growing rx-fcs-error / rx-align-error = cable or connector problem.

commands.name: Who uses the bandwidth on a port right now
commands.use: Live list of addresses and their traffic. Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.name: Port up/down history
commands.use: When ether2 restarts, the times show here.

commands.name: Turn on loop protection for a port
commands.use: Router disables the port briefly and logs 'loop detected' when a loop appears behind it.

commands.name: Turn on RSTP (loop-safe bridge)
commands.use: Blocks loops between switches automatically (2-3 s LAN pause when applied).

commands.name: Restart a port (reboots PoE device behind it)
commands.use: Camera / AP hanging.

commands.name: Block a device (no internet, no other networks)
commands.cmd: :do {/ip firewall filter add chain=forward src-mac-address={mac} action=drop comment="ND block {mac}" place-before=([/ip firewall filter find]->0)} on-error={/ip firewall filter add chain=forward src-mac-address={mac} action=drop comment="ND block {mac}"}
commands.use: Cuts internet for a device that is attacking or misbehaving.

commands.name: Unblock a device
commands.cmd: /ip firewall filter remove [find where comment="ND block {mac}"]

commands.name: Neighbours (switches / APs the router sees)
commands.use: Identity, model and port of MikroTik / CDP / LLDP devices - use to tag switches.

commands.name: Router CPU, memory, uptime
commands.use: CPU near 100% = the router is the bottleneck (or a flood / attack). Low uptime = it rebooted (power?).

commands.name: Router errors in the log
commands.use: Recent problems the router itself noticed.

commands.name: Cable test of a port (find the break)
commands.use: Shows each wire pair and roughly how many metres away a cable is broken (on models that support it).

commands.name: Live traffic of one device
commands.use: What this device is talking to right now and how fast. Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.name: Ping from the router
commands.use: If the router can ping it but a PC can't, the problem is between that PC and the switch.

commands.name: Limit the speed of one device
commands.cmd: :do {/queue simple remove [find name="ND limit {ip}"]} on-error={}; /queue simple add name="ND limit {ip}" target={ip}/32 max-limit={limit}/{limit} comment="ND {mac}"
commands.use: E.g. limit 5M. Stops one PC / camera eating the whole internet line. If the limit seems ignored: FastTrack (on in the default setup) skips speed limits - use 'Turn off FastTrack' below.

commands.name: Turn off FastTrack (so speed limits work)
commands.use: Speed limits and per-device traffic counting need it off. The router CPU works harder - check 'Router CPU, memory, uptime' afterwards. Undo: the same with 'enable'.

commands.name: Fix websites that hang (MSS clamp)
commands.cmd: /ip firewall mangle add chain=forward protocol=tcp tcp-flags=syn action=change-mss new-mss=clamp-to-pmtu passthrough=yes comment="ND: MSS clamp"
commands.use: For PPPoE / VPN lines with MTU below 1500 (Tools > MTU finder).

commands.name: Use fast public DNS on the router
commands.use: After Tools > DNS server test. Make sure the firewall drops DNS (port 53) coming from the internet side.

commands.name: DHCP leases (all devices)
commands.use: Every address the router gave out; 'D' = dynamic, no D = reserved (bound).

commands.name: Is the DHCP pool full?
commands.use: Compare with the pool size (/ip pool print). A full pool = new devices get no IP (169.254.x.x).

commands.name: Services open on the router (security)
commands.use: Turn off what you don't use: /ip service disable telnet,ftp,api,api-ssl. Never leave WinBox open to the internet.

commands.name: Who logged in to the router
commands.use: Logins and failed logins - unknown IPs = someone is guessing the password.

commands.name: Back up the router settings
commands.use: Then download nd-backup.rsc / .backup from WinBox > Files. Do it before big changes.

commands.name: Ping a device
commands.use: Ctrl+C to stop.

commands.name: Cable speed of the Mac
commands.use: 1000baseT = gigabit. 100baseTX on a cable = damaged cable / old switch.

commands.name: Wi-Fi details
commands.use: Signal, channel, speed of the Wi-Fi.

commands.name: Devices with a driver problem (yellow mark)
commands.use: Lists every device Windows has a problem with (missing / failed driver). Same as the yellow marks in Device Manager.

commands.name: All installed driver packages
commands.use: Driver packages in the Windows driver store with version and date.

commands.name: Search Windows Update for missing drivers (scan)
commands.use: Starts a Windows Update scan, which also finds drivers. Open Settings > Windows Update after a minute.

commands.name: Open Windows Update
commands.use: Install pending updates and optional driver updates (Advanced options > Optional updates).

commands.name: Programs with a newer version (winget)
commands.use: Lists installed programs that have an update (Windows 10 / 11 with App Installer).

commands.name: Update all programs (winget)
commands.use: Updates Chrome, Zoom, 7-Zip, AnyDesk ... in one go. Run as administrator.

commands.name: Dell: install Dell Command Update
commands.use: Dell's own driver / BIOS updater. Then use the next command.

commands.name: Dell: scan and apply all driver updates
commands.use: Installs every Dell driver and BIOS update for this model (needs Dell Command Update).

commands.name: Lenovo: install Lenovo System Update
commands.use: Lenovo's driver / BIOS updater for ThinkPad, ThinkCentre, IdeaPad.

commands.name: HP: install HP Support Assistant
commands.use: HP's driver updater. Business PCs can use HP Image Assistant instead.

commands.name: PC maker, model and serial (for the driver page)
commands.cmd: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Select Manufacturer,Model; (Get-CimInstance Win32_BIOS).SerialNumber"
commands.use: Dell service tag / Lenovo / HP serial number to type on the maker's driver page.

commands.name: Last Windows updates installed
commands.use: When this PC was last updated. Older than 1-2 months = check Windows Update.

commands.name: Network card driver version
commands.use: Old network drivers cause drops and slow Wi-Fi; compare with the maker's page.

commands.name: Reset Windows Update (when it is stuck)
commands.cmd: net stop wuauserv && net stop bits && ren %windir%\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old && net start bits && net start wuauserv
commands.use: Fixes Windows Update errors / stuck downloads (admin). The old folder can be deleted later.

commands.name: Repair Windows system files
commands.use: Repairs damaged Windows files (admin, 10-30 minutes). For crashes and updates that fail.

commands.name: Printers installed and their ports
commands.use: Which printer uses which IP / port and driver.

commands.name: Clear a stuck print queue
commands.cmd: net stop spooler && del /q /f %windir%\System32\spool\PRINTERS\* && net start spooler
commands.use: Jobs stuck in the queue, 'printing' forever (admin).

commands.name: Add a network printer by IP
commands.use: Creates the port for the printer at {ip}; then Add-Printer -Name 'Office' -DriverName '<name from the list>' -PortName 'IP_{ip}'.

commands.name: Is the printer's print port open? (9100)
commands.use: TcpTestSucceeded True = the printer accepts print jobs.

commands.name: Which antivirus is installed and is it on?
commands.cmd: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/SecurityCenter2 -ClassName AntivirusProduct | Select displayName,productState,timestamp"
commands.use: Every antivirus Windows knows (Defender, Quick Heal, K7, ESET, Seqrite ...). The PC details script decodes on / off and up to date.

commands.name: Windows Defender status
commands.use: Real-time protection on? Signatures from today or yesterday?

commands.name: Windows Defender: update signatures now
commands.use: Downloads the newest virus definitions.

commands.name: Windows Defender: quick scan
commands.use: 5-15 minutes. Results: Get-MpThreatDetection.

commands.name: Windows Defender: threats found
commands.use: What Defender found and removed / quarantined.

commands.name: Windows Defender: offline scan (restarts the PC)
commands.use: For malware that hides while Windows runs. The PC restarts and scans for ~15 minutes.

commands.name: Quick Heal / Seqrite: is the service running?
commands.cmd: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "Get-Service | Where {$_.DisplayName -match 'Quick Heal|Seqrite'} | Select DisplayName,Status"
commands.use: Status Running = protection active. Update from the Quick Heal / Seqrite window (or the Seqrite EPS console).

commands.name: K7 / ESET / Kaspersky / McAfee: service status
commands.use: Shows whether the third-party antivirus services are running.

commands.name: ESET: update and scan from the command line
commands.use: ESET command-line scanner (path differs on older ESET versions).

commands.name: Firewall on / off for each network type
commands.use: Domain, Private, Public should normally all be ON.

commands.name: Turn the firewall ON (all profiles)
commands.cmd: netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state on
commands.use: Admin. Someone turned it off 'to make something work' - turn it back on and allow only that program.

commands.name: Allow a TCP port in
commands.cmd: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Allow TCP {tcpport}" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport={tcpport}
commands.use: For a server program (ERP, Tally 9000, SQL 1433, RDP 3389) that other PCs must reach.

commands.name: Allow ping (ICMP) in
commands.cmd: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Allow ping" dir=in action=allow protocol=icmpv4:8,any
commands.use: So Network Doctor and others can ping this PC.

commands.name: Turn on file and printer sharing
commands.cmd: netsh advfirewall firewall set rule group="File and Printer Sharing" new enable=Yes
commands.use: Shared folders / printers on this PC not reachable from other PCs.

commands.name: Firewall rules that block
commands.cmd: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "Get-NetFirewallRule -Action Block -Enabled True | Select DisplayName,Direction,Profile"
commands.use: A block rule can stop a program even when the firewall 'allows' it elsewhere.

commands.name: Reset the firewall to Windows defaults
commands.use: Removes all custom rules (admin). Last resort when rules are a mess.

commands.name: Which port is a MAC on?
commands.use: The MAC in Cisco form xxxx.xxxx.xxxx. The port column tells where the device is plugged in.

commands.name: Port status, speed, duplex
commands.use: a-full a-1000 = good. a-half or a-100 on a PC port = cable problem.

commands.name: Port errors (CRC = bad cable)
commands.use: CRC / FCS / Align errors that keep growing = replace the cable or the port.

commands.name: Neighbours (which switch is on which port)
commands.use: LLDP instead: show lldp neighbors detail.

commands.name: Loop / spanning tree check
commands.use: Topology changes going up all the time = a loop or a port flapping. 'show spanning-tree detail | inc ieee|from' shows where.

commands.name: Shut / restart a port
commands.cmd:
configure terminal
interface {iface}
shutdown
no shutdown
end
commands.use: Restarts a port (e.g. Gi1/0/5). Leave out 'no shutdown' to keep it off.

commands.name: Put a port in a VLAN
commands.use: Access port for a PC / phone / camera in one VLAN.

commands.name: Stop loops: BPDU guard + storm control on PC ports
commands.cmd:
configure terminal
interface range {iface}
spanning-tree portfast
spanning-tree bpduguard enable
storm-control broadcast level 5
end
write memory
commands.use: A port with a loop or a home router plugged in shuts itself down instead of taking the network down.

commands.name: DHCP snooping (stop rogue DHCP)
commands.cmd:
configure terminal
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan {vlan}
interface {iface}
ip dhcp snooping trust
end
write memory
commands.use: {iface} = the uplink to the real router - only that port may answer DHCP.

commands.name: Send logs to Network Doctor (syslog)
commands.cmd:
configure terminal
logging host {lip}
logging trap warnings
end
write memory
commands.use: Port up / down, loops and errors appear in the Live monitor.

commands.name: SNMP read access for Network Doctor
commands.cmd:
configure terminal
snmp-server community netdoctor RO
end
write memory
commands.use: Lets Network Doctor read the MAC table and port traffic (community netdoctor).

commands.name: NetFlow to Network Doctor (Cisco router)
commands.cmd:
configure terminal
flow exporter ND
 destination {lip}
 transport udp 2055
flow monitor NDM
 exporter ND
 record netflow ipv4 original-input
interface {iface}
 ip flow monitor NDM input
end
commands.use: Per-device / per-site traffic in the Live monitor. {iface} = the LAN interface.

commands.name: Save the configuration
commands.use: Changes are lost at the next power cut without this.

commands.name: Which port is a MAC on?
commands.use: MAC with colons. Web UI: MAC Address > Address Table.

commands.name: Port status and speed
commands.use: Check speed / duplex. Web UI: Switching > Port > Port Config.

commands.name: Port errors
commands.use: Growing error / CRC counters = cable or port problem.

commands.name: Loop detection on all ports
commands.cmd:
configure
loopback-detection
interface range gigabitEthernet 1/0/1-24
loopback-detection
loopback-detection config process-mode port-based recovery-mode auto
end
copy running-config startup-config
commands.use: Blocks a port that has a loop and opens it again later. Web UI: Switching > Loopback Detection.

commands.name: Put a port in a VLAN
commands.use: {iface} like 1/0/5.

commands.name: DHCP snooping (stop rogue DHCP)
commands.cmd:
configure
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan {vlan}
interface gigabitEthernet {iface}
ip dhcp snooping trust
end
copy running-config startup-config
commands.use: {iface} = the uplink to the real router.

commands.name: Syslog to Network Doctor
commands.cmd:
configure
logging host index 1 {lip} 4
end
copy running-config startup-config
commands.use: Port and loop events in the Live monitor.

commands.name: SNMP read access
commands.cmd:
configure
snmp-server
snmp-server community netdoctor read-only
end
copy running-config startup-config
commands.use: Network Doctor reads the MAC table and traffic. Omada-managed: set it in the Omada controller (Site > Services > SNMP).

commands.name: Reserve an IP / bind IP-MAC
commands.cmd: Open http://{gw} > Network / Transmission > DHCP > Address Reservation (ER series: Preferences > IP-MAC Binding). Add MAC {mac} -> IP {ip}.
commands.use: TP-Link routers have no command line for this - use the web page.

commands.name: Block a website
commands.cmd: Open http://{gw} > Firewall / Security > Access Control (ER series: Behavior Control > URL filtering). Add the domain.
commands.use: Or point the office DNS to this PC's website firewall (Tools).

commands.name: Which port is a MAC on?
commands.use: Newer DGS-1250/1510 (Cisco-like CLI): show mac-address-table address {mac_dash}.

commands.name: Port status, speed, errors
commands.use: Half duplex / 100M on a PC port or growing CRC errors = cable.

commands.name: Loop detection on
commands.cmd:
enable loopdetect
config loopdetect ports all state enabled
config loopdetect recover_timer 60
save
commands.use: Shuts a looping port and reopens it after 60 s.

commands.name: Put a port in a VLAN
commands.use: {iface} = port number, e.g. 5.

commands.name: Syslog + SNMP for Network Doctor
commands.cmd:
enable syslog
create syslog host 1 ipaddress {lip} severity warning state enable
create snmp community netdoctor view CommunityView read_only
save
commands.use: Logs and MAC table for Network Doctor.

commands.name: Which port is a MAC on?
commands.use: MAC in xxxxxx-xxxxxx form also works.

commands.name: Port status and errors
commands.use: Look at 'FCS Rx' and 'Drops'.

commands.name: Loop protection
commands.cmd:
configure
loop-protect 1-24
loop-protect trap loop-detected
write memory
commands.use: Blocks a looping port.

commands.name: Syslog + SNMP
commands.cmd:
configure
logging {lip}
snmp-server community netdoctor operator
write memory
commands.use: For Network Doctor.

commands.name: UniFi device: info and controller address
commands.use: SSH to the UniFi switch / AP. 'set-inform http://<controller>:8080/inform' adopts it.

commands.name: UniFi switch: which port is a MAC on?
commands.use: Or the UniFi controller > Clients.

commands.name: EdgeRouter: DHCP leases
commands.use: Names and IPs of all devices.

commands.name: EdgeRouter: NetFlow to Network Doctor
commands.cmd:
configure
set system flow-accounting interface eth1
set system flow-accounting netflow server {lip} port 2055
set system flow-accounting netflow version 9
commit; save
commands.use: eth1 = the LAN port. Per-device traffic in the Live monitor.

commands.name: Which port is a MAC on?
commands.use: Smart (web-only) models: Switching > Address Table.

commands.name: Port status
commands.use: Speed / duplex for every port.

commands.name: Loop / broadcast storm protection
commands.cmd:
configure
storm-control broadcast level 5
keepalive
exit
write memory
commands.use: Web UI: Security > Traffic Control > Storm Control.

commands.name: Which port is a MAC on?
commands.use: Huawei MAC form xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.

commands.name: Port status and errors
commands.use: Look at CRC and duplex.

commands.name: Loop detection
commands.cmd:
system-view
loopback-detect enable
interface {iface}
loopback-detect enable
return
save

commands.name: Who is using the internet now (top sessions)
commands.cmd:
diagnose sys top-summary
get system performance status
commands.use: CPU, memory, sessions. GUI: Dashboard > FortiView Sources.

commands.name: Sessions of one device
commands.cmd:
diagnose sys session filter src {ip}
diagnose sys session list
commands.use: What the device {ip} is connected to. Clear the filter: diagnose sys session filter clear.

commands.name: DHCP leases
commands.use: Names / IPs / MACs.

commands.name: Test the internet from the firewall
Syslog to Network Doctor
commands.cmd:
config log syslogd setting
set status enable
set server {lip}
end
commands.use: Traffic and security logs in the Live monitor.

commands.name: NetFlow to Network Doctor
commands.cmd:
config system netflow
set collector-ip {lip}
set collector-port 2055
end
config system interface
edit {iface}
set netflow-sampler both
end
commands.use: Per-device / per-site traffic. {iface} = LAN interface (e.g. internal / port1).

commands.name: Block a device (address + deny policy)
commands.cmd:
config firewall address
edit "ND-block-{ip}"
set subnet {ip} 255.255.255.255
next
end
commands.use: Then add a deny policy for it at the top (GUI: Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy).

commands.name: Console: ping / traceroute / ARP
commands.use: Device console (SSH, option 4 Device Console).

commands.name: Syslog to Network Doctor
commands.cmd: Web admin: System services > Log settings > Add syslog server {lip} UDP 514, then tick the log types.

commands.name: States (connections) of a device
commands.use: Shell (option 8). What {ip} is connected to now.

commands.name: DHCP leases
commands.use: GUI: Status > DHCP Leases.

commands.name: NetFlow / syslog to Network Doctor
commands.cmd: GUI: pfSense - install softflowd, host {lip} port 2055; Status > System Logs > Settings > Remote log {lip}:514. OPNsense - Reporting > NetFlow.

commands.name: Syslog to Network Doctor
commands.cmd: Web admin: Logs & Reports > Settings > Syslog server {lip} port 514.

commands.name: Find a device's switch port without a login
commands.cmd: Network Doctor > Tools > Switch port finder (SNMP community netdoctor), or unplug-and-watch with 'ping -t {ip}'.
commands.use: Works with any SNMP switch (Cisco, TP-Link, D-Link, HP, Netgear, Huawei).

insights.title: Still learning
insights.text: No usage recorded yet. It needs NetFlow from the router (Setup > Router commands) and the Live monitor running. Names of websites come from the router's DNS cache (router login in Setup) or the website firewall.
